description: This radial chart visually represents the composition of analysis layers within a speech, audio, and music reasoning framework, showing three main concentric rings corresponding to three primary layers: the outermost "Content Analysis" layer, the middle "Perception Layer," and the innermost "Semantic Layer." The chart displays a total of 13 distinct segments or categories distributed across these layers. The largest segment, occupying approximately 40.4% of the middle ring, is labeled "Perception Layer." The next largest segment, at 41.2%, is the "Semantic Layer" in the outer ring. The smallest segment, at 4.3%, is the "Signal Layer" within the middle ring. The outermost "Content Analysis" layer is composed of several smaller segments including "Emotion & Intention," "Speaker Analysis," "Content Analysis" (which appears to be a label for the entire outer ring), and others. The middle ring includes "Environmental Perception & Reasoning," "Counting & Statistics," "Music Theory," "Correlation Analysis," "Temporal Analysis," "Spatial Analysis," "Professional Knowl & Reasoning," "Culture of Speaker," "Imagination," "Acoustic Quality Analysis," "Anomaly Detection," and "Aesthetic Analysis." The chart includes percentage labels directly on the segments for the "Perception Layer," "Semantic Layer," and "Signal Layer," and uses a color gradient from light to dark blue to differentiate between layers, with the outermost ring being a lighter blue than the middle ring. There is no legend, and no segments are visually emphasized (e.g., exploded or bolded). The segments appear to be arranged in descending order of size within each ring, though the exact order is not strictly uniform across all rings.
